title: School Scrabble Grandmaster Finals & Novices
summary: The School Scrabble Grandmaster Finals & Novices was concluded successfully at the Public Library of Colombo.
content: The Inaugural School Scrabble Grandmaster Finals and Novices Tournament was successfully held on 14th February at the Public Library of Colombo, marking a historic milestone in the development of school Scrabble in Sri Lanka. For the first time in Sri Lankan Scrabble, five different categories were contested on a single day. These included the Under-20 Finals, Under-16 Finals, Under-12 Finals, Open Novices, and Under-12 Novices, creating a vibrant and competitive atmosphere throughout the venue. The finalists were selected from collective qualifying tournaments held across the Western and Central Provinces in the previous year, setting the stage for high-quality competition in every category. The Under-20 and Under-16 Finals were played over nine nationally rated rounds, while the Under-12 Finals featured six rounds. Both Novices categories competed in five games each, providing valuable competitive exposure for emerging players. The tournament was directed/ adjudicated and officiated by an experienced panel comprising Raashid Sudin, Kavindu Malawaraarachchi, Imeth De Silva, Ramith Siriwardana, Nishanya Gammanpila, and Zainab Sultan. For the first time in the country, the tournament featured 5 categories with over 150 players participating, the event ran smoothly from start to finish, a testament to the dedication and hard work of the officials and organizers. The tournament not only showcased the growing depth of young Scrabble talent in Sri Lanka but also set a strong foundation for future school-level championships.

title: Med Fest Scrabble Tournament - University of Colombo
summary: Directing the Med Fest Scrabble Tournament of the University of Colombo
content: The Scrabble tournament organized by the Medical Faculty of the University of Colombo as part of its Med Fest celebrations was held on 18th February at the UCFM Tower, offering a refreshing and fun take on competitive Scrabble. Three batches: 2022, 2023, and 2024 competed in both Men’s and Women’s categories, with the event being adjudicated and directed by Imeth De Silva. The competition began at 6.00 p.m. and continued until 9.30 p.m., following a three-round round-robin format. The concept of night Scrabble added to the excitement, creating a lively atmosphere and making the games both intense and enjoyable. At the conclusion of the tournament, the Batch of 2022 emerged champions in the Men’s category, while the Batch of 2024 claimed the Women’s title. With great vibes, enthusiastic participation, and smooth organization, the Med Fest Scrabble tournament highlighted the growing Scrabble culture within the University of Colombo and demonstrated how innovative formats can make the game even more engaging at the university level.

title: Workshop at University of Peradeniya
summary: A Scrabble workshop for beginners was successfully conducted at University of Peradeniya on 31st January
content: The Sri Lanka Scrabble Academy helped organized an Introductory workshop and tournament at the University of Peradeniya on 31st January, marking another important step in expanding Scrabble within Sri Lanka’s university community. The workshop was conducted by Raashid Sudin, President of the Sri Lanka Scrabble Academy, together with the Academy’s Secretary, Imeth De Silva. The session was organized by Shamil Rashaad, the University Scrabble Captain at the University of Peradeniya, whose initiative brought together an enthusiastic group of students eager to learn and experience the game. The programme began with an introductory workshop designed to familiarize participants with the fundamentals of competitive Scrabble. Key areas covered included strategic thinking, teamwork, and effective decision-making on the board. Following the introduction, university students paired into teams of two and competed against other pairs in an American School Scrabble–style format for the very first time in Sri Lanka. This format encouraged collaboration, learning through play, and healthy competition. There were some interesting team names such as Ravenclaw, Zyzzyvas, Scammers, Sakura, Kavi,  Panda, Team Q, Electric Scalpers etc etc....While Team Panda won the tournament, Ravenclaw secured the Runners up position and 2nd runners up was Scammers.....Sri Lanka Scrabble Academy is committed to introducing new tournament formats to the country to add flair to already a growing scrabble community...The atmosphere throughout the session was lively and engaging, with students quickly adapting to the format and embracing Scrabble as both a mental challenge and a social activity. The mini tournament added excitement to the programme, reinforcing the idea that Scrabble can be both educational and enjoyable. The workshop concluded on a high note, reflecting a successful introduction to Scrabble at the University of Peradeniya and reaffirming the Sri Lanka Scrabble Academy’s commitment to promoting and developing the game across universities throughout the country.

title: Workshop at Springfield College Kandy
summary: A Scrabble workshop for beginners was successfully conducted at Springfield College on 14th January
content: A Scrabble workshop for beginners was successfully conducted at Springfield College on 14th January, introducing students to a fresh and strategic approach to the game of Scrabble. The session saw over 40 participants from Springfield College, Kandy, enthusiastically taking part. Designed especially for beginners, the workshop focused on building a strong foundation in Scrabble, moving beyond basic word formation to a more structured and strategic understanding of the game. Participants were introduced to key concepts such as board awareness, rack management, scoring strategies, and efficient word selection — helping them view Scrabble not just as a word game, but as a competitive mind sport. The workshop was conducted by Raashid Sudin, President of the Sri Lanka Scrabble Academy, whose engaging and practical teaching approach helped students grasp new strategies with ease. The Springfield College workshop marked another important step in the Academy’s ongoing efforts to promote Scrabble at educational institutions and to nurture young players by equipping them with modern techniques and strategic insight into the game.
